inclusive support model

Source record: docs/studies/analysis/pulsechain_local_pls_support_20260929.md.
Finite pDAI exits into PLS: a fee-inclusive support model
29 September 2026. Mathematical research only. The holder receives native PLS on PulseChain, or WPLS
assumed exchangeable one-for-one with native PLS. No Ethereum exit, external-dollar redemption or
cross-chain withdrawal is required by this model. The PLS dollar reference is only the unit used to
measure the local result. Actual wrapper and historical trade evidence are separate from these
illustrative reserves and trading fees.
Result
The conditional argument can be strengthened beyond a single price quote. In the explicit model below,
an initial purchase plus a finite PLS support budget funds thirty successive local exits, each selling 1,000
pDAI for 10 million PLS. At the stipulated reference of $0.0001 per PLS, each holder receives $1 of locally
valued PLS per pDAI. Both trade directions charge a 0.3% input fee retained in the pool. This is a
constructed finite scenario, not an estimate of PulseChain market cost or a probability of success.
The same model also identifies failures when the budget is smaller, seller flow doubles, or the PLS
reference falls. This makes the claim bounded and testable rather than assuming a permanent peg from
one successful trade.
Model and equations
Let x and y be the pool's pDAI and PLS reserves. Let b be gross PLS spent buying pDAI; g = 1 − buy_fee.
Actual post-purchase reserves are:
x1 = x × y / (y + g × b)
y1 = y + b.
The entire input remains in the pool; the fee-adjusted input determines output. Consequently, the
product of actual reserves grows when a positive fee is retained. Reusing the fee-free constant-product
terminal identity would be wrong. This is the conventional input-fee treatment described by the Uniswap
v2 primary white paper. The selected fee is illustrative, not a claim about PulseX, Curve or Balancer.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 299

For a holder subsequently selling gross q pDAI, let h = 1 − sale_fee. The PLS output and dollar-reference
execution value are:
z = y1 × h × q / (x1 + h × q)
execution value = s × z / q, where s is the PLS dollar reference.
For target T, the sufficient initial input is the nonnegative solution of A × b² + B × b + C = 0, where:
A = s × g
B = s × y × (1 + g) − T × q × g
C = s × y² − T × q × y − T × x × y / h
b = (−B + sqrt(B² − 4 × A × C)) / (2 × A)
Use b = 0 if the existing finite-sale quote already satisfies the target. The implementation uses equal buy/
sale fees; the displayed derivation permits different fees. It uses 80-digit Decimal arithmetic, not EVM
integer rounding.
Explicit experiment
Initial reserves are 1,000,000 pDAI and 1,000,000,000 PLS; initial reference is $0.0001 per PLS. T arget is
$1 of PLS per pDAI on the specified sale. The initial purchase establishes a quote for a 1,000-pDAI exit. It
is separately funded; the support budget in the table is additional PLS inventory.
Before each of thirty seller events, the treasury computes the purchase needed for that event's trade
size and reference. It executes that purchase only if its remaining PLS covers the full amount. Otherwise
it makes no partial purchase, and the holder still sells at the resulting market quote. The policy is chosen
to expose sufficiency and failure thresholds, not to optimize real execution.
No other trades, liquidity changes, debt payments or replenishment occur. Gas, wrapping and other
transaction costs are funded separately and excluded. The model assumes timely intervention before
each specified event; it does not prove a continuous price floor during arbitrary interleaved trading.

For the 0.3%-fee, constant-reference, 1,000-pDAI scenario:
Initial purchase: 2,175,295,195.262100 PLS, receiving approximately 684,420.069032 pDAI.
Additional purchases before events 2–30: 290,871,239.738011 PLS.
• 
• 
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 300

Holders receive 300,000,000 PLS in total for 30,000 pDAI.
Treasury support remaining: 109,128,760.261989 PLS.
Operator final pDAI inventory: approximately 713,333.206430 pDAI.
There are 29 restoration purchases, because the initial purchase funds the first target quote. The
calculation does not restore a fresh target quote after the thirtieth sale. The displayed remaining budget
is unspent support inventory, not profit: substantial PLS was paid for pDAI, whose future sale is not
modeled.
The fee-free control reproduces the earlier initial purchase of 2,167,281,613.012984 PLS and requires
290,000,000 additional PLS across the same 29 restoration purchases. Fees raise both acquisition and
intervention costs.
Conservation and funding interpretation
At every event the experiment checks:
pool pDAI + operator pDAI
    = initial pool pDAI + cumulative seller pDAI input
pool PLS + remaining support PLS + cumulative holder PLS received
    = initial pool PLS + initial purchase PLS + initial support PLS
It also checks nonnegative cash and reserves, nondecreasing reserve product with retained fees, and
achievement of the target whenever the calculated full intervention is funded. Local sellers exchange
their pDAI for existing PLS. No bridge-out cash flow appears anywhere in these identities.
One of the paper's financing mechanisms could supply the initial purchase or support treasury. This
model does not establish which deployed mechanism does so. Receipt sales, funded loans, eligible issuer
trades or relayer delivery must supply net spendable PLS, or executable alternative purchasing assets,
without counting settlement reserves twice. A loan-funded treasury also needs its debt maturity and
repayment accounted for in any extended horizon.
A constant PLS/pDAI exchange ratio can satisfy a fixed PLS target even when the dollar reference falls. It
cannot simultaneously preserve the same dollar-valued target without adjustment. The event-16 failure
tests that distinction without requiring holders to sell PLS externally.
Appreciation and the sell-above-target side
A fresh batch, pulsechain_local_pls_appreciation_20260929.json, uses the same thirty-event model with a 1.5×
or 2× reference increase at event 16. Both branches keep all thirty holder exits at or above the target
while spending approximately 140,420,598.446934 additional support PLS. The buy-only policy stops
buying when the quote exceeds the lower bound; it does not restore exact equality. Those successes
therefore establish a local minimum execution value, not an exact peg after appreciation. The two
branches share the same token flows because neither needs further buying within this finite horizon.
A separate sell-side checkpoint makes the two-sided intuition concrete. It starts after event 15 of the
constant-reference, 0.3%-fee baseline, with 698,378.135367209278 pDAI owned by the operator and
259,579,401.553066 PLS of remaining support treasury. The operator is assumed to own that pDAI free
of pledges or other commitments. There is no intervening trade or liquidity change.
Let a be the operator's gross pDAI sale, with input-fee factor h. Starting at this checkpoint's reserves x,y,
the sale leaves:
• 
• 
• 
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 301

x1 = x + a, y1 = x × y / (x + h × a).
For the next holder sale of q, restoring its execution value to T requires:
(x + h × a) × (x + a + h × q) = s × h × x × y / T.
Solve the quadratic with coefficients:
A = h
B = x × (1 + h) + h² × q
C = x × (x + h × q) − s × h × x × y / T
a = (−B + sqrt(B² − 4 × A × C)) / (2 × A)
This branch applies when the existing holder quote is above target. The required sale must fit the
operator's available pDAI. The operator receives y × h × a / (x + h × a) PLS from the pool; this changes
ownership of existing PLS rather than creating native units.
Assumed reference Operator pDAI sale PLS received by operator Next 1,000-pDAI holder's
PLS output
$0.00015 (+50%) 70,153.484465 572,788,016.391764 6,666,666.666667
$0.0002 (+100%) 130,138.650678 920,191,644.708543 5,000,000
Both inventory checks pass; the next holder receives exactly $1 of reference-valued PLS per pDAI. The
operator's resulting PLS inventory is 832,367,417.944829 or 1,179,771,046.261608 respectively. These
alternatives cannot be added together or treated as profits independent of the pDAI sold. The operator
still retains approximately 628,224.650902 or 568,239.484689 pDAI.
The economic review independently confirmed both roots using 450 bisection iterations at 110-digit
precision and checked conservation. This higher precision checks arithmetic, not additional precision in
the original checkpoint. The checkpoint establishes one sell-above-target response, not stability under
every future price path. No causal model here predicts that the peg raises PLS.
The separate manifest is Research/experiments/pulsechain_local_pls_rebalance_20260929.json; its source
checkpoint and hash are embedded. Run the corresponding script with a new path:
python Research/scripts/model_local_pls_rebalance.py \
  --manifest Research/experiments/pulsechain_local_pls_rebalance_20260929.json \
  --output artifacts/pulsechain-local-pls-rebalance-reproduction
Recorded outputs are under artifacts/pulsechain-local-pls-rebalance-20260929/; the appreciation buy-only
outputs are under artifacts/pulsechain-local-pls-appreciation-20260929/. Earlier batches and their script
hashes remain unchanged.
Reproduction and limits
Run from the repository root with a fresh output directory:
python Research/scripts/model_local_pls_support.py \
  --manifest Research/experiments/pulsechain_local_pls_support_20260929.json \
  --output artifacts/pulsechain-local-pls-support-reproduction
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 302

The recorded batch is artifacts/pulsechain-local-pls-support-20260929/. It preserves inputs, per-event results
and source/input/output hashes. It does not modify the older fee-free experiment. The script has no
network access or signing capability. No chain simulation or transaction was performed.
This is a scenario result, not a statistical success rate. It does not cover all market venues, adversarial
timing, new liquidity, native-PLS supply changes, LP exits, rebasing or fee-on-transfer tokens, oracle
failures or liquidity-provider responses. The specified inventory, seller flow and reference path are the
boundaries of the positive result. A stronger local-support claim must specify and evaluate those
additional conditions rather than assume them away.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 303
